claim: For the \(4\times4\) grid graph \(G(4,4)=P_4\mathbin{\square}P_4\), the \(10\)-cut complex \(\Delta_{10}(G(4,4))\) has \(\widetilde H_4(\Delta_{10}(G(4,4));\mathbb F_2)\cong\mathbb F_2^4\) and \(\widetilde H_5(\Delta_{10}(G(4,4));\mathbb F_2)\cong\mathbb F_2^{2747}\), with all other reduced mod-\(2\) homology groups zero. Hence this pure \(5\)-dimensional complex is not shellable, so \((m,n,k)=(4,4,10)\) is a counterexample to Bayer--Denker--Jelić Milutinović--Sundaram--Xue Conjecture 5.9 that \(\Delta_k(G(m,n))\) is shellable for every \(3\le k\le mn-3\).
integrity: The finite claim is reproduced from the graph and cut-complex definitions by an embedded standalone verifier using exhaustive enumeration, two face-generation routes, two rank computations, boundary-square checks, and an Euler-characteristic check.
scientific_limitations: The result computes homology only over \(\mathbb F_2\) and uses it solely to obstruct shellability. It does not determine integral homology or homotopy type and makes no minimality claim among grid counterexamples.
title: The \(4\times4\) grid refutes all-\(k\) cut-complex shellability
